title: Data generation and analysis with SIRIUS 4 on two biological case studies
protocol: Dispose of ethanol:water 1:1 (v/v) from swab container.
Replace with fresh ethanol:water 1:1 (v/v).
Prepare a 96-well plate by adding 500 µL of solvent mix to each well.
Place the 96-well plate on an ice bed.
Take one swab and vigorously swab the spot of interest for at least five seconds.
Place the swab into the corresponding well of the 96-well plate.
Cut the swab with scissors, leaving only the cotton bud in the well.
Dispose of the swab wood stick.
Cover the rest of the plate with aluminium foil to prevent cross-contamination during handling.
Close the 96-well plate with a polypropylene reusable cover.
Leave the 96-well plate with soaked cotton buds at 4°C for 24 to 48 hours.
Remove each cotton bud with tweezers, pressing the bud on the side of the well to retrieve solvent.
Cover other wells with aluminum film during this step.
Evaporate the solvent content in the 96-well plate using a benchtop vacuum centrifuge concentrator.
Redissolve the plate content in 120 μL of 1:1 (v/v) acetonitrile:water at ambient temperature.
Cover the plate with a lid and agitate gently, then use an ultrasonic bath for 5 min.
Centrifugate the 96-well plate at 2000 rpm for 15 minutes at ambient temperature.
Transfer 100 μL of the plate content into a new 96-well plate using a multi-channel pipette.
Cover the plate with aluminium foil to avoid contamination.
Place each swab onto a Thermo Fisher Scientific 2-ml deep-well 96-well plate set on top of dry ice coolant.
Discard the top part of each swab stick.
Add 200 µl of HPLC-grade 90% ethanol-water solvent to each well using a multichannel pipette.
Seal the plate with a 96-well plate lid.
Sonicate the plate for 10 min.
Place the plate into the refrigerator at 2°C to extract samples overnight.
Remove and discard swabs from the wells.
Place the plates into a lyophilizer.
Dry down the entire sample in the lyophilizer.
Add 200 μl of 90% ethanol-water solution for resuspension.
Seal the plates and centrifuge at 2,000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Transfer 100-μl aliquots of the sample onto a Falcon 96-well MS plate using a multichannel pipette.
Seal the plate immediately with sealing film.
Centrifuge the sealed plates at 2,000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Prepare LC mobile phase A as 100:0.1 (v/v) water:formic acid.
Prepare LC mobile phase B as 100:0.1 (v/v) acetonitrile:formic acid.
Prime the C18 HPLC column according to the manufacturer's guidelines.
Set up the LC linear gradient method with a flow rate of 500 μL/min.
Set up the LC parameters including column temperature at 40°C and loop factor wash as appropriate for the system.
Inject samples into the system with volumes of 10 μL for skin samples or 5 μL for fecal samples.
Calibrate instruments using the calibration solution according to manufacturer's guidelines.
Add the solution containing internal lockmass m/z 922.009 in the ESI source for the MaXis II QTOF in positive ion mode.
Set up the MS method as follows: acquire spectra in positive ion mode with a mass range of m/z 80 to 2,000 on the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Configure capillary voltage at 4,500 V for the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Set ion source temperature to 180 °C for the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Adjust dry gas flow to 9 L/min for the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Acquire spectra at a rate of 3 spectra per second using the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Perform MS/MS fragmentation of the seven most intense selected ions per spectrum (TOP7) using ramped collision-induced dissociation (CID) energy ranging from 16 to 48 eV for the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Set MS/MS exclusion after 3 spectra to be released after 30 seconds for the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Exclude ions in the mass range of m/z 921.5 to 924.5 from MS/MS analysis on the MaXis II QTOF MS.
Consider including other adducts of the lockmass if their intensities are within the MS/MS threshold for exclusion on the MaXis II QTOF MS.

Run a blank sample and verify that no significant contamination impacts the system by assessing ion abundances and ensuring they do not exceed instrument thresholds (e.g., below few thousand counts for the MaXis II QTOF).
Consider additional source cleaning, replacement of mobile phases, glassware, LC column or tubing if high abundance contaminants are present.
Run the QC sample.
Follow the QC sample with a blank.
Repeat steps starting with running the QC sample at least two times.
Inspect multiple QC samples to ensure reproducibility (coefficient of variation below 0.1-0.3).
Check for carryover by inspecting the blank that follows each QC sample.
Adjust injection volume if necessary to prevent chromatographic or detector saturation.
Optimize LC gradient for appropriate separation of features and number of needle/injector washes to reduce carry-over below 1%.
Prepare LC-MS sequence including analysis of a blank and QC sample every 12 samples.
Randomize the order of samples if possible.
Include a clean-up sample every 12 samples if necessary to limit column saturation.
Run the LC-MS sequence.
Monitor regularly that elution profile of each QC sample is reproducible (5-10 sec window maximum for UHPLC or coefficient of variation below 0.1-0.3).
Calibrate the LC-MS instrument according to manufacturer guidelines if needed.
Add lock mass calibrant every 12 hours for MaXis II QTOF.
Run a QC sample and a blank prior to continuing analysis after calibration.
Open representative files from both beginning and end of the sequence with MS data viewing software.
Overlap features across samples, including the internal standard.
Assess stability of chromatography (retention shift in seconds).
Assess stability of MS calibration (m/z window in ppm).
Export all LC-MS/MS files into centroided .mzXML format.
Use CompassXport to apply calibration and convert data from .d format to .mzXML format in centroid mode.
Convert collected HPLC-MS raw data files from Bruker's .d format to .mzXML format.
Set alignment window at 0.5 min, noise threshold at 1000 counts, chromatographic peak full width at half-maximum (FWHM) value at 20, and mass error at 30 ppm for feature detection.
Remove peaks present in any of the blanks with a signal-to-noise ratio below 10:1 from the final feature table.
Convert collected HPLC-MS raw data files from Bruker's .d format to .mzXML format.
Load experimental files and batch-process them with mass detection settings including noise level at 1000, minimum peak height at 3000, m/z tolerance at 20 ppm or 0.1 m/z.
Process chromatogram builder step with minimum time span at 0.01 min and minimum peak height at 3000.
Apply chromatogram deconvolution settings including baseline cutoff with minimum peak height at 3000, peak duration range from 0.01 to 3.00 minutes, and baseline level at 300.
Perform isotopic peak grouping in the deisotopisation step with m/z tolerance set at 20 ppm or 0.1 m/z.
Set required library matches to have a score above 0.7.
Require at least 6 matched peaks for library matches.
Search spectra in the network against GNPS spectral libraries.
Download the GraphML file for Cytoscape from the generated GNPS job status page.
Open Cytoscape software and import the downloaded .graphml file.
Select appropriate labels for network nodes and edges under the Style tab.
Postulate molecular structures of compounds using annotation propagation from adjacent annotated nodes in clusters.
Assess differences in parent mass and fragmentation patterns to postulate structures.
(Optional) Procure authentic standards for level 1 identifications if possible.
Compare retention times and MS/MS spectra of authentic standards to experimentally obtained data.
Extract the MS/MS spectrum of the compound using MSConvert software.
Launch MSConvert GUI.
Click "Browse" and select the experimental .mzXML file containing the MS/MS spectrum of interest.
Click "Add" to include the file into the analysis window.
Click "Browse" for the "Output Directory" field to select the output directory.
Select "Output format": mgf.
Select "Binary encoding precision": 32 bit.
Uncheck "Use zlib compression".
Under "Filters", select "Subset" and enter the scan number of the MS/MS spectrum of interest.
Click "Add".
Click "Start".
The .mgf file containing the single MS/MS will be saved in the selected output folder.
When viewing the network cluster on GNPS, select the node of interest by left clicking it.
Click on the "Download MS/MS Peaks" icon to download the .txt file.
Launch the GUI of the SIRIUS software.
Import the MS/MS spectrum for analysis.
Click the "Import" icon.
Click the "+" icon.
Select the file with MS/MS of interest (enter parent m/z if not recognized from the file).
Alternatively, click the "Batch Import" icon.
For single spectrum import, select the ionization mode [M+H]+.
Click "Compute All".
In the pop-up window, select "Elements beside CHNOP": include sulfur; for the range of expected number of atoms use up to "+2".
Select instrument: "Q-TOF".
Set ppm: 20.
Keep candidates at default of 10.
In the drop down menu, select "formulas from biological databases".
Click the "CSI:FingerID" button.
Under "Search in", select "biological database".
Select possible adducts ([M+H]+ is selected by default).
Click "Compute".
